give me a unified exception report: whic:
SELECT 'LATE_ROUTE' AS exception_type, d.route_id::VARCHAR AS entity_id, COALESCE(rt.route_name, d.route_id::VARCHAR) AS entity_name,
               'Delivery delayed ' || d.delay_minutes || ' mins' AS detail
        FROM clean_db_deliveries d
        LEFT JOIN clean_db_routes rt ON d.route_id=rt.route_id
        WHERE d.delay_minutes > 120 AND d.dispatch_datetime >= (SELECT MAX(dispatch_datetime) FROM clean_db_deliveries) - INTERVAL 1 DAY
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'LOW_FILL' AS exception_type, f.outlet_id::VARCHAR AS entity_id, o.outlet_name AS entity_name,
               ROUND(AVG(f.fill_rate_cases)*100,1) || '% fill rate' AS detail
        FROM mart_financial_service f
        JOIN clean_db_outlets o ON f.outlet_id=o.outlet_id
        WHERE f.order_date >= (SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM mart_financial_service) - INTERVAL 1 DAY
        GROUP BY 2,3 HAVING AVG(f.fill_rate_cases) < 0.80

which 5 general trade outlets have seen:
WITH m1 AS (
            SELECT outlet_id, COUNT(*) AS c1 FROM clean_db_orders WHERE order_date >= (SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM clean_db_orders)-INTERVAL 6 MONTH AND order_date < (SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM clean_db_orders)-INTERVAL 3 MONTH GROUP BY 1
        ), m2 AS (
            SELECT outlet_id, COUNT(*) AS c2 FROM clean_db_orders WHERE order_date >= (SELECT MAX(order_date) FROM clean_db_orders)-INTERVAL 3 MONTH GROUP BY 1
        )
        SELECT o.outlet_name, COALESCE(m1.c1,0) AS older_orders, COALESCE(m2.c2,0) AS recent_orders,
               COALESCE(m2.c2,0) - COALESCE(m1.c1,0) AS delta
        FROM clean_db_outlets o
        LEFT JOIN m1 ON o.outlet_id=m1.outlet_id
        LEFT JOIN m2 ON o.outlet_id=m2.outlet_id
        WHERE o.channel = 'General Trade'
        ORDER BY delta ASC LIMIT 5
